Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0 npm Release Drops Rust Infostealer During Install

The Hacker News
2026-07-11 13 use cases 5 techniques 5 kill-chain phases detected

The jscrambler npm package was compromised, and simply installing its&nbsp;8.14.0&nbsp;release runs an infostealer on your machine. Published on July 11, 2026, the malicious version carries a&nbsp;preinstall&nbsp;hook that drops and executes a native binary, one build each for Windows, macOS, and Linux. Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Tampered jscrambler@8.14.0 package files (dist/setup.js, dist/intro.js) written to node_modules
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Compromised jscrambler 8.14.0 npm Release Drops Rust Infostealer During Install
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] npm preinstall hook (node.exe) launches detached hidden binary from temp directory · [LLM] Every-minute relaunch of hidden temp binary via Task Scheduler (jscrambler stealer persistence) · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] jscrambler stealer C2 beacon to 37.27.122.124 / 57.128.246.79 and Tor bootstrap · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Temp-dir binary harvesting cloud/browser/AI-tool secrets after jscrambler install · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
Tampered jscrambler@8.14.0 package files (dist/setup.js, dist/intro.js) written to node_modules AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the specific supply-chain artifact: the two malicious files added only in jscrambler 8.14.0 (dist/setup.js loader and the 7.8MB dist/intro.js binary container) landing under node_modules/jscrambler, matched by their published SHA-256. Fires on install/restore of the poisoned release before the payload even runs. Rationale: Anchors on the two file SHA-256s and the exact node_modules/jscrambler/dist path that StepSecurity and SafeDep both confirmed are unique to 8.14.0 and absent from the upstream GitHub repo, so any hit is the poisoned release, not a benign jscrambler install. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/jscrambler-npm-package-publishes-malicious-preinstall-binary • https://safedep.io/jscrambler-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A security researcher deliberately pulling 8.14.0 into a sandbox for analysis
  • A mirror/proxy registry (Artifactory/Verdaccio) caching the malicious tarball on a build host
  • Restoring an old lockfile pinned to 8.14.0 in a CI cache-warm job
  • Forensic imaging tools re-writing the file during evidence collection (path-only branch)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("mdatp","windowsdefender") or FolderPath has @"\quarantine\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SHA-256 match and identify the host/CI runner and the user/service account that ran the install; pull package-manager logs for jscrambler@8.14.0. 2) Contain: isolate the host, remove node_modules/jscrambler and the tarball from caches, repin to 8.13.0 or 8.15.0, and purge lockfiles referencing 8.14.0. 3) Hunt: if present, treat all reachable secrets as stolen — check for temp-dir binary execution, the two C2 IPs, and persistence artifacts on this and any host sharing the lockfile.

npm preinstall hook (node.exe) launches detached hidden binary from temp directory AIInstallation High
Hunts the execution step of the jscrambler compromise: setup.js, run by the preinstall lifecycle hook, writes the platform payload under a random hidden name in the system temp dir and launches it detached with output suppressed. Detects a node/npm parent spawning a hidden .{random}(.exe) child out of a temp path, or any process matching the three published payload hashes. Rationale: Pairs the article's exact behavioral chain (node/npm preinstall -> hidden random-name binary in temp, launched detached) with the three confirmed payload SHA-256s, so it fires on both the known hashes and the technique even if the attacker re-rolls the binary. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/jscrambler-npm-package-publishes-malicious-preinstall-binary • https://safedep.io/jscrambler-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1204.003 T1059.007 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • node-gyp / native-addon builds writing transient binaries under Temp during install
  • Electron or puppeteer downloading a browser/helper into a temp cache and exec-ing it
  • node-based test runners spawning helper executables from os.tmpdir()
  • postinstall scripts of legitimate packages (esbuild, swc, sharp) extracting prebuilt binaries
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild-install","esbuild","@swc","sharp") and SHA256 !in ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd","b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903","c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: inspect InitiatingProcessCommandLine for setup.js / jscrambler / preinstall and the child SHA-256; confirm the temp binary is unsigned and hidden. 2) Contain: kill the process tree, isolate the host, and quarantine the temp binary; rotate any secret reachable by the install account. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same SHA-256 and the two C2 IPs across the fleet and CI runners; check Task Scheduler (Windows) and ~/Library/LaunchAgents (macOS) for persistence pointing at temp.

jscrambler stealer C2 beacon to 37.27.122.124 / 57.128.246.79 and Tor bootstrap AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts the network stage: the dropped Rust binary beacons over TLS to two hard-coded attacker IPs and reaches Tor bootstrap infrastructure (check.torproject.org / archive.torproject.org). Any host contacting these two IPs is high-confidence compromise; the Tor bootstrap clause corroborates on hosts where the IP hit was missed. Rationale: Uses the two hard-coded C2 IPs and the two Tor bootstrap FQDNs that StepSecurity's Harden-Runner captured at runtime — the first published network IOCs for the campaign, independently listed by SafeDep — making an IP hit effectively a true positive. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/jscrambler-npm-package-publishes-malicious-preinstall-binary • https://safedep.io/jscrambler-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1573.002 T1090.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate Tor Browser user on a dev workstation hitting check.torproject.org (Tor clause only)
  • Threat-intel enrichment/sandbox detonation infrastructure reaching the C2 IPs deliberately
  • A shared-hosting IP (Hetzner/OVH ranges) later reassigned to a benign service
  • Security scanners probing the C2 IPs from a jump host
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("tor.exe","firefox.exe","tor-browser.exe") and RemoteUrl in~ ("check.torproject.org","archive.torproject.org"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process — a temp-dir binary confirms the stealer; correlate to a recent jscrambler@8.14.0 install on the same host. 2) Contain: block 37.27.122.124 and 57.128.246.79 at the egress firewall/proxy, isolate the host, and kill the process. 3) Hunt: assume exfil succeeded — rotate all cloud, npm, GitHub, AI-tool/MCP keys and revoke browser/Bitwarden/Slack/Discord sessions for users on the host; sweep the fleet for the two IPs and the payload hashes.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("37.27.122.124","57.128.246.79")
   or RemoteUrl in~ ("check.torproject.org","archive.torproject.org")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("37.27.122.124","57.128.246.79")
| project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, NetworkApplicationProtocol, DvcAction
| union (
    ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery in~ ("check.torproject.org","archive.torproject.org")
    | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname=DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber=int(null), NetworkApplicationProtocol="dns", DvcAction=DnsQuery
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Every-minute relaunch of hidden temp binary via Task Scheduler (jscrambler stealer persistence) AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the Windows persistence the payload wires in: a hidden scheduled task set to relaunch the temp-dir binary every minute. Detects Task Scheduler service (svchost/taskeng) repeatedly launching a hidden .{random}(.exe) child from a temp path at high frequency — the signature of the minute-interval task surviving reboot. Rationale: Targets the article's specific persistence detail — a hidden scheduled task relaunching every minute — via the anomalous high-frequency Task Scheduler launch of a hidden temp binary, a shape no legitimate app produces from os.tmpdir(). Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/jscrambler-npm-package-publishes-malicious-preinstall-binary • https://safedep.io/jscrambler-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1564.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An installer/updater temporarily registering a per-minute task from Temp during a rollout
  • A misbehaving software watchdog re-launching a helper from Temp in a tight loop
  • QA/automation harnesses running a scheduled job pointed at a temp build artifact
  • Antivirus re-scanning and re-invoking a quarantined temp file (parent would be AV, filtered)
Suppression filter
| where not (SHA256 in (known_good_updater_hashes)) and FileName matches regex @"^\.[A-Za-z0-9]+(\.exe)?$"
Response runbook
1) Triage: enumerate Task Scheduler for hidden tasks with a 1-minute trigger pointing at Temp (schtasks /query /v or the TaskCache registry); capture the binary SHA-256. 2) Contain: disable/delete the task, kill the process, quarantine the temp binary, and isolate the host. 3) Hunt: correlate to a jscrambler@8.14.0 install and the two C2 IPs; on macOS hosts inspect ~/Library/LaunchAgents for a matching login-persistence plist.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("svchost.exe","taskeng.exe")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\")
| where FileName matches regex @"^\.[A-Za-z0-9._-]+(\.exe)?$"
| summarize Runs=count(), FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), SampleCmd=any(ProcessCommandLine) by DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, bin(Timestamp, 1h)
| where Runs >= 10   // minute-interval task => ~60 launches/hr; 10 well above benign scheduled jobs
| order by Runs desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4698   // scheduled task created
| where EventData has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\")
| where EventData has "PT1M" or EventData has "Minute"   // one-minute repetition interval
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, TaskContent=EventData
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Temp-dir binary harvesting cloud/browser/AI-tool secrets after jscrambler install AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the collection stage: a single non-browser process (the dropped temp binary) reading across disparate secret stores — cloud CLI creds (~/.aws, Azure, gcloud), browser credential DBs, the Bitwarden vault, and the newer AI coding-tool/MCP config files (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, VS Code, Zed). Fan-out across 3+ distinct secret classes by one temp process is the stealer's signature. Rationale: Combines the temp-dir stealer process with the article's explicit target list — cloud CLI creds, browser Login Data, Bitwarden, and the distinctive AI-tool/MCP config files (Claude/Cursor/Windsurf/VS Code/Zed) — requiring 2+ secret classes to fire, which no benign single-purpose tool does. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/jscrambler-npm-package-publishes-malicious-preinstall-binary • https://safedep.io/jscrambler-npm-supply-chain-compromise/
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1552.001 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A backup/sync agent (OneDrive, backup software) reading many user config files
  • A legitimate dev-environment migration tool copying .aws, VS Code, and browser profiles
  • Endpoint DLP/inventory scanners enumerating credential files
  • A password-manager desktop app legitimately reading its own vault (filtered by temp-process requirement)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("onedrive.exe","backup.exe","code.exe","bitwarden.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !has @"\Temp\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the reading process is an unsigned temp-dir binary (not a known backup/DLP agent) and list which secret classes it touched. 2) Contain: isolate the host and kill the process; immediately rotate every credential class it read — cloud keys, npm/GitHub tokens, AI-tool/MCP API keys — and revoke browser/Bitwarden/Slack/Discord sessions. 3) Hunt: correlate to jscrambler@8.14.0 install and outbound traffic to 37.27.122.124/57.128.246.79; check whether CI metadata endpoints (169.254.169.254) were queried from the same process.
let SecretPaths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", @"\.config\gcloud\", @"\.azure\", @"\Login Data", @"Bitwarden", @"\Claude\", @"\Cursor\", @"\Windsurf\", @"\.codeium\", @"\Zed\", @"\Code\User\"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\", "/tmp/", "/var/folders/")
| where FolderPath has_any (SecretPaths)
| extend Class = case(
    FolderPath has_any (@"\.aws", "gcloud", @"\.azure"), "cloud",
    FolderPath has_any (@"Login Data", "Bitwarden"), "vault",
    FolderPath has_any (@"\Claude", @"\Cursor", @"\Windsurf", @"\.codeium", @"\Zed", @"\Code\User"), "aitool",
    "other")
| summarize DistinctClasses=dcount(Class), Classes=make_set(Class), Files=make_set(FolderPath), Reads=count() by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| where DistinctClasses >= 2   // one temp process touching 2+ secret categories = stealer fan-out
| order by Reads desc
let SecretPaths = dynamic([@"\.aws\credentials", "gcloud", @"\.azure\", @"\Login Data", "Bitwarden", @"\Claude\", @"\Cursor\", @"\Windsurf\", @"\.codeium\", @"\Zed\", @"\Code\User\"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\Windows\Temp\", "/tmp/", "/var/folders/")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (SecretPaths)
| extend Class = case(
    TargetFilePath has_any (@"\.aws", "gcloud", @"\.azure"), "cloud",
    TargetFilePath has_any (@"Login Data", "Bitwarden"), "vault",
    TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Claude", @"\Cursor", @"\Windsurf", @"\.codeium", @"\Zed", @"\Code\User"), "aitool",
    "other")
| summarize DistinctClasses=dcount(Class), Classes=make_set(Class), Reads=count() by DvcHostname, ActingProcessName
| where DistinctClasses >= 2
| order by Reads desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @Image:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\.* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\.*) @TargetFilename:(*\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\gcloud\\* OR *\\.azure\\* OR *\\Login\ Data OR *Bitwarden* OR *\\Claude\\* OR *\\Cursor\\* OR *\\Windsurf\\* OR *\\Zed\\* OR *\\Code\\User\\*)
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo | ContextImageFileName=/\\(AppData\\Local\\Temp|Windows\\Temp)\\\./i | TargetFileName=/(\.aws\\credentials|gcloud|\.azure|Login Data|Bitwarden|Claude|Cursor|Windsurf|codeium|Zed|Code\\User)/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName], function=count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true)) | _count >= 2
CLOUD

| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*","/tmp/*","/var/folders/*")) AND (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\.aws\\credentials","*\\.config\\gcloud\\*","*\\.azure\\*","*\\Google\\Chrome\\*\\Login Data","*\\Microsoft\\Edge\\*\\Login Data","*\\Bitwarden*","*\\Claude\\*","*\\Cursor\\*","*\\Windsurf\\*","*\\.codeium\\*","*\\Zed\\*","*\\Code\\User\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | eval secret_classes=mvcount(mvdedup(mvmap(paths, case(match(paths,"(?i)\.aws|gcloud|\.azure"),"cloud", match(paths,"(?i)Login Data|Bitwarden"),"vault", match(paths,"(?i)Claude|Cursor|Windsurf|codeium|Zed|Code\\User"),"aitool", true(),"other")))) | where secret_classes >= 2 | sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.process_path IN ("*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*","*\\Windows\\Temp\\*","/tmp/*","/var/folders/*")) AND (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*\\.aws\\credentials","*\\.config\\gcloud\\*","*\\.azure\\*","*\\Google\\Chrome\\*\\Login Data","*\\Microsoft\\Edge\\*\\Login Data","*\\Bitwarden*","*\\Claude\\*","*\\Cursor\\*","*\\Windsurf\\*","*\\.codeium\\*","*\\Zed\\*","*\\Code\\User\\*")) by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | eval secret_classes=mvcount(mvdedup(mvmap(paths, case(match(paths,"(?i)\.aws|gcloud|\.azure"),"cloud", match(paths,"(?i)Login Data|Bitwarden"),"vault", match(paths,"(?i)Claude|Cursor|Windsurf|codeium|Zed|Code\\User"),"aitool", true(),"other")))) | where secret_classes >= 2 | sort - count
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`

title: Scheduled Task Creation with Suspicious Image / Encoded Args
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0d
status: experimental
description: |
    schtasks.exe /create with payload-shaped action — points at
    powershell, cmd, rundll32, encoded-base64, or user-writable paths.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1053/005/

    - attack.execution

    category: process_creation
    product: windows

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium

Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or SHA1 in~ ("a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or MD5 in~ ("a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or SHA1 in~ ("a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or MD5 in~ ("a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,

| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["a742de963f14a92d24ebcbc7b44ac867e23a20d31d1b0094a13a4f83287f4e60", "a41a523ef9517aab37ed6eea0ec881821bdcb7aefcb5c5f603adc7907f868c86", "fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

cms_plugin.exe Rust stager execution + payload pull from 193.42.25.65 AIInstallation High
Hunts the custom 'cms_plugin.exe' implant that masqueraded as a Complaint Management System portal update on Balochistan Police infrastructure. The Rust stager variant downloads a next stage from 193.42.25.65 and prints 'Update Complete! Please refresh the page'. Fires on the named binary executing or any host reaching the stager download IP. Rationale: cms_plugin.exe is a unique implant filename and 193.42.25.65 is the confirmed Rust-stager download server named in the SentinelLABS report; both are non-generic, so a match is effectively a true positive. Cross-checked SentinelOne report and The Record write-up. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/one-target-china-india-espionage-converge-on-pakistani-law-enforcement/ • https://therecord.media/china-india-ran-separate-spy-campaigns-against-same-police-force
ATT&CKT1105 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimately-named plugin binary in an unrelated product also called cms_plugin.exe (rare; validate hash and path)
  • Security researcher / IR analyst detonating the sample in a sandbox VM enrolled in EDR
  • Threat-intel enrichment appliance actively probing 193.42.25.65 for research
  • Proxy/NAT egress IP collision where 193.42.25.65 is re-used by a benign CDN in future (validate at trigger time)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\Sandbox\\" and DeviceName !in~ ("IR-SANDBOX-01")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the process tree, SHA256, and folder path for cms_plugin.exe; confirm parent (likely w3wp.exe/web-app service on a CMS/web server) and whether the host is an internet-facing police web application server. 2) Contain: isolate the host, block 193.42.25.65 at the perimeter, and preserve the binary for reversing. 3) Hunt: sweep all web servers for cms_plugin.exe uploads, search web logs on cms.balochistanpolice.gov.pk-style portals for the file, and pivot on the SHA1s and the full campaign C2 IP set (see C2 UC).
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP == "193.42.25.65" or InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "cms_plugin.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
union
(SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where tolower(NewProcessName) endswith "\\cms_plugin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, Signal="process", NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, Dest=""),
(CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP == "193.42.25.65"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, Account=SourceUserName, Signal="network", NewProcessName=ProcessName, CommandLine="", ParentProcessName="", Dest=DestinationIP)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Balochistan Police cms_plugin.exe Implant Execution
id: 6b1f2c9a-4d3e-4a11-9c77-2f0b8e5a1d42
description: Detects execution of the custom cms_plugin.exe implant deployed against Pakistani law enforcement (SentinelLABS).
references:
  - https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/one-target-china-india-espionage-converge-on-pakistani-law-enforcement/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/11
tags:
  - attack.t1105
  - attack.t1036.005
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\cms_plugin.exe'
  selection_orig:
    OriginalFileName: 'cms_plugin.exe'
  condition: selection or selection_orig
level: high
source:windows.sysmon (@EventID:3 @DestinationIp:193.42.25.65) OR (@EventID:1 @Image:(*\cms_plugin.exe OR *\CMS_Plugin.exe OR *\CMS_PLUGIN.EXE))
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4="193.42.25.65"
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, RemotePort], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="cms_plugin.exe" OR Processes.original_file_name="cms_plugin.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name="cms_plugin.exe" OR Processes.original_file_name="cms_plugin.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Fake 360Safe.exe (.NET) reflectively loading AsyncRAT AIInstallation Medium
Hunts the second cms_plugin.exe variant: a .NET executable that masquerades as '360Safe.exe' (a legitimate Qihoo 360 Total Security binary) to reflectively load an in-memory AsyncRAT client. Detects a process named 360Safe.exe whose file metadata is NOT Qihoo/360 or which runs from outside the legitimate 360 install path. Rationale: The report states one implant variant masquerades specifically as 360Safe.exe (Qihoo 360) to reflectively load AsyncRAT; a 360Safe.exe binary running outside the genuine Qihoo install path (or lacking Qihoo file metadata) is a high-fidelity masquerade signal, especially in a Pakistani gov environment unlikely to run Chinese AV. Corroborated by SentinelOne report and Kaspersky's Mysterious Elephant AsyncRAT/Remcos tradecraft. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/one-target-china-india-espionage-converge-on-pakistani-law-enforcement/ • https://securelist.com/mysterious-elephant-apt-ttps-and-tools/117596/
ATT&CKT1036.005 T1620
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine Qihoo 360 Total Security installed to a non-default drive/path (validate publisher signature)
  • Portable/standalone 360 Total Security run from a USB or Downloads folder by a user
  • Software-deployment tool staging the real 360Safe.exe in a temp cache before install
  • AV bake-off / procurement testing of 360 Total Security by IT
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("360","Qihoo"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: check the digital signature and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName of the 360Safe.exe image — genuine is signed by Qihoo/360; the implant will be unsigned or mis-signed. Inspect for .NET/CLR module loads and outbound connections. 2) Contain: isolate the host, capture memory (AsyncRAT is in-memory), block associated C2 IPs. 3) Hunt: search DeviceImageLoadEvents for clr.dll/mscoree loading into 360Safe.exe, and correlate with cms_plugin.exe drops and the campaign C2 IP set.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "360Safe.exe"
| where not(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has_any ("360","Qihoo")) or FolderPath !startswith "C:\\Program Files"
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, ProcessVersionInfoProductName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where tolower(NewProcessName) endswith "\\360safe.exe"
| where not(tolower(NewProcessName) startswith "c:\\program files (x86)\\360\\") and not(tolower(NewProcessName) startswith "c:\\program files\\360\\")
| where Account !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
title: Masquerading 360Safe.exe Outside Qihoo 360 Install Path
id: 8c2d4e17-9a55-4b3e-8f21-1d7c6b0e4a99
description: Detects a process named 360Safe.exe running from a non-standard path, consistent with the AsyncRAT loader used against Balochistan Police (SentinelLABS).
references:
  - https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/one-target-china-india-espionage-converge-on-pakistani-law-enforcement/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/11
tags:
  - attack.t1036.005
  - attack.t1620
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\360Safe.exe'
  filter_legit:
    Image|startswith:
      - 'C:\Program Files (x86)\360\'
      - 'C:\Program Files\360\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @Image:(*\360Safe.exe OR *\360safe.exe OR *\360SAFE.EXE) -@Image:(C:\Program?Files?(x86)\360\* OR C:\Program?Files\360\*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ImageFileName=/\\360safe\.exe$/i
| NOT (ImageFileName=/\\Program Files( \(x86\))?\\360\\/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="360Safe.exe" NOT (Processes.process_path="C:\\Program Files (x86)\\360\\*" OR Processes.process_path="C:\\Program Files\\360\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="360Safe.exe" NOT (Processes.process_path="C:\\Program Files (x86)\\360\\*" OR Processes.process_path="C:\\Program Files\\360\\*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing to Balochistan Police espionage C2 / stager IP set AICommand & Control High
Hunts outbound connections to the confirmed command-and-control and staging IPs across the four converging clusters (Cobalt Strike C2 142.171.183.8, Rust-stager host 193.42.25.65, plus the campaign infrastructure block) targeting Pakistani law enforcement. Any internal host reaching these IPs warrants investigation. Rationale: 142.171.183.8 is the named Cobalt Strike C2 and 193.42.25.65 the stager host; the remaining IPs are the pre-extracted campaign infrastructure. These are static, second-source-consistent IOCs, so egress to any of them is high-fidelity for this specific converging-actor campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/one-target-china-india-espionage-converge-on-pakistani-law-enforcement/ • https://therecord.media/china-india-ran-separate-spy-campaigns-against-same-police-force
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • An IOC IP later reassigned to a shared hosting/CDN provider serving benign sites (re-validate WHOIS at trigger time)
  • Internal threat-intel platform or vulnerability scanner actively probing the C2 IPs
  • Security researcher pivoting on the infrastructure from a corporate egress IP
  • Firewall/proxy that logs a blocked (denied) attempt — confirm DeviceAction/outcome is allow before escalating
Suppression filter
DeviceNetworkEvents | where ActionType in ("ConnectionSuccess","ConnectionAttempt") and RemoteIPType == "Public"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the source host and the InitiatingProcess making the connection; check whether the connection succeeded vs was blocked, and beacon regularity (jitter/interval). 2) Contain: block all listed IPs at the perimeter, isolate any host with a successful/repeated connection, and snapshot memory for the process (PlugX/ShadowPad/Cobalt Strike/AsyncRAT are memory-resident). 3) Hunt: pivot on the initiating process hash against the campaign SHA1 list, sweep for cms_plugin.exe and fake 360Safe.exe, and review the FortiMail email gateway and web-app servers for the initial foothold.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("142.171.183.8","193.42.25.65","41.216.188.140","89.31.121.220","45.125.32.218","172.111.233.36","172.111.233.96","172.111.233.12","172.111.233.105","172.111.233.26","172.94.9.49","172.94.9.43","172.94.9.19","45.74.6.17")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), Conns=count(), Ports=make_set(RemotePort,10) by DeviceName, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by LastSeen desc
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DestinationIP in ("142.171.183.8","193.42.25.65","41.216.188.140","89.31.121.220","45.125.32.218","172.111.233.36","172.111.233.96","172.111.233.12","172.111.233.105","172.111.233.26","172.94.9.49","172.94.9.43","172.94.9.19","45.74.6.17")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), Conns=count(), Ports=make_set(DestinationPort,10) by SourceIP, SourceHostName, DestinationIP, DeviceProduct
| order by LastSeen desc
title: Balochistan Police Espionage Campaign C2 IP Contact
id: 3f9a1c2b-7e64-4d0a-b3c1-9e2f5a8d7c10
description: Detects network connections to confirmed C2 / staging IPs from the multi-cluster espionage campaign against Pakistani law enforcement (SentinelLABS).
references:
  - https://www.sentinelone.com/labs/one-target-china-india-espionage-converge-on-pakistani-law-enforcement/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/11
tags:
  - attack.t1071.001
  - attack.t1105
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    DestinationIp:
      - '142.171.183.8'
      - '193.42.25.65'
      - '41.216.188.140'
      - '89.31.121.220'
      - '45.125.32.218'
      - '172.111.233.36'
      - '172.111.233.96'
      - '172.111.233.12'
      - '172.111.233.105'
      - '172.111.233.26'

level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationIp:(142.171.183.8 OR 193.42.25.65 OR 41.216.188.140 OR 89.31.121.220 OR 45.125.32.218 OR 172.111.233.36 OR 172.111.233.96 OR 172.111.233.12 OR 172.111.233.105 OR 172.111.233.26 OR 172.94.9.49 OR 172.94.9.43 OR 172.94.9.19 OR 45.74.6.17)
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 RemoteAddressIP4=/^(142\.171\.183\.8|193\.42\.25\.65|41\.216\.188\.140|89\.31\.121\.220|45\.125\.32\.218|172\.111\.233\.(36|96|12|105|26)|172\.94\.9\.(49|43|19)|45\.74\.6\.17)$/

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=t count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("142.171.183.8","193.42.25.65","41.216.188.140","89.31.121.220","45.125.32.218","172.111.233.36","172.111.233.96","172.111.233.12","172.111.233.105","172.111.233.26","172.94.9.49","172.94.9.43","172.94.9.19","45.74.6.17") by All_Traffic.src_ip All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic where All_Traffic.dest_ip IN ("142.171.183.8","193.42.25.65","41.216.188.140","89.31.121.220","45.125.32.218","172.111.233.36","172.111.233.96","172.111.233.12","172.111.233.105","172.111.233.26","172.94.9.49","172.94.9.43","172.94.9.19","45.74.6.17") by All_Traffic.src_ip All_Traffic.dest_ip All_Traffic.dest_port All_Traffic.app | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)` | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("142.171.183.8", "193.42.25.65", "41.216.188.140", "89.31.121.220", "45.125.32.218", "172.111.233.36", "172.111.233.96", "172.111.233.12", "172.111.233.105", "172.111.233.26", "172.94.9.49", "172.94.9.43", "172.94.9.19", "45.74.6.17") or RemoteUrl has_any ("cms.balochistanpolice.gov.pk")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["142.171.183.8", "193.42.25.65", "41.216.188.140", "89.31.121.220", "45.125.32.218", "172.111.233.36", "172.111.233.96", "172.111.233.12", "172.111.233.105", "172.111.233.26", "172.94.9.49", "172.94.9.43", "172.94.9.19", "45.74.6.17"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["cms.balochistanpolice.gov.pk"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Url, NetworkProtocol
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("cms.balochistanpolice.gov.pk")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append

        where DNS.query IN ("cms.balochistanpolice.gov.pk")

| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime

| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`

        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("cms.balochistanpolice.gov.pk")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]

jscrambler npm package publishes malicious preinstall binary

StepSecurity
2026-07-11 14 use cases 5 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

On July 11, 2026, version 8.14.0 of jscrambler was published to npm carrying a malicious preinstall hook that drops and executes a platform-specific native binary on Linux, Windows, and macOS. jscrambler is the official CLI client for the Jscrambler Code Integrity API, a commercial JavaScript obfuscation and web-app protection service, with a clean version history dating back to 0.1.0. The compromised release was flagged by StepSecurity's AI Release Analyzer with a suspicion score of 0 (the maximum suspicion rating) on publish.

Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Temp-dropped binary reading browser credential and wallet vault stores · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs · Crypto-wallet file/keystore access by non-wallet process
Malicious jscrambler 8.14.0 binary container dropped as node_modules/jscrambler/dist/intro.js AIDelivery High
Hunts the write of the 7.8 MB custom binary container disguised as intro.js under the jscrambler package dist folder, the smuggled Rust payload carrier for jscrambler@8.14.0. This is the on-disk artifact that confirms the compromised release landed on a host or CI runner. Rationale: Anchors on the exact package-specific path node_modules/jscrambler/dist/intro.js from the IOC table — a file that has no legitimate function in a JS-obfuscation CLI, making a match near-conclusive for the compromised 8.14.0 install.
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1027.009
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer manually re-creating a file literally named intro.js under a jscrambler dist folder for testing (extremely rare)
  • Security researcher storing a copy of the malicious tarball unpacked in that path for analysis
  • Backup/restore tooling replaying an old node_modules tree containing the artifact
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the parent package version — check package-lock.json/node_modules/jscrambler/package.json for 8.14.0 and compute the SHA256 of intro.js. 2) Contain: isolate the host/CI runner, kill any orphaned temp-dir process, and pin jscrambler to 8.13.0 in the lockfile. 3) Hunt: sweep all build agents and dev laptops for the same path, then pivot to the C2 IPs and browser-credential-store access UCs to gauge whether the stealer payload ran.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "intro.js"
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\jscrambler\dist\" or FolderPath has "/node_modules/jscrambler/dist/"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, FileSize, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "intro.js"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\jscrambler\dist\" or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/jscrambler/dist/"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

jscrambler preinstall loader (node.exe) spawns detached executable from OS temp dir AIInstallation High
Hunts the preinstall loader behaviour where dist/setup.js, running under node during npm install, decompresses the platform payload to a randomly named dotfile in the OS temp directory (.exe on Windows) and launches it detached. Detects node spawning an executable living in the temp directory whose name begins with a dot. Rationale: Combines the article's stated loader behaviour (node running setup.js drops a dot-prefixed random file to the OS temp dir and executes it) into a parent=node + child-in-temp-starting-with-dot pivot that no benign npm install exhibits.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1204.001 T1036.008
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm packages that compile and execute native postinstall helpers from temp (rare, and they seldom use dot-prefixed names)
  • Electron/node-gyp build steps writing scratch executables to temp
  • Antivirus sandbox detonating node payloads in a temp workspace
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp","prebuild-install","electron-builder"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the temp executable's SHA256 and compare against the three known payload hashes; note the parent node command line to confirm it references jscrambler/dist/setup.js. 2) Contain: kill the orphaned/unref'd temp process (it survives npm exit), quarantine the temp binary, and isolate the host. 3) Hunt: pivot on the process's outbound connections to the C2 IPs and Tor domains, and check for browser credential-store reads.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", "/tmp/", "/var/folders/")
| where FileName startswith "."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ParentProcessName in~ ("node.exe","node")
| where TargetProcessName has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", "/tmp/", "/var/folders/")
| extend LeafName = tostring(split(replace_string(TargetProcessName, "/", "\\"), "\\")[-1])
| where LeafName startswith "."
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Known jscrambler stealer payload SHA256 executed or written on host AIInstallation Medium
High-fidelity alerting on the exact ELF/PE/Mach-O payloads extracted from jscrambler 8.14.0's intro.js container, by SHA256, across process-execution and file-write telemetry. A direct hash hit is definitive compromise regardless of how the file arrived. Rationale: Uses the three verbatim payload SHA256 values from the IOC table across both execution and file-write surfaces; a hash match is unambiguous and platform-complete (Linux/Windows/macOS).
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware sample stored/analyzed in a research VM triggering a file-write hit
  • EDR test/detonation of the sample by the SOC itself
  • Threat-intel enrichment tooling caching the binary on a scanning host
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm Source (execution vs file-write) and the initiating command line; execution means the stealer ran. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process, and treat as fully compromised per the vendor guidance. 3) Hunt: rotate every browser-stored credential and audit crypto-wallet extensions on that host, then pivot to the C2-egress UC for exfiltration confirmation.
let PayloadHashes = dynamic(["fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd","b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903","c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd"]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (PayloadHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, Source="ProcessExec", Path=FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine),
  (DeviceFileEvents | where Timestamp > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (PayloadHashes) | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, Source="FileWrite", Path=FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let PayloadHashes = dynamic(["fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd","b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903","c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd"]);
union
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where SHA256 in (PayloadHashes) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source="ProcessExec", TargetProcessName, SHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine),
  (ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where TargetFileSHA256 in (PayloadHashes) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, Source="FileWrite", TargetProcessName=TargetFilePath, SHA256=TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Outbound C2 from jscrambler stealer to hardcoded IPs and Tor endpoints AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts direct connections to the two C2 IPs (37.27.122.124, 57.128.246.79) and the archive/check.torproject.org endpoints observed from the dropped binary via Harden-Runner monitoring. Scopes to build/dev hosts where these destinations are anomalous, indicating the stealer beaconing or fetching Tor tooling. Rationale: Uses the two Harden-Runner-captured C2 IPs and the two torproject FQDNs from the article; on a CI runner or dev host these destinations are highly anomalous and directly tie network activity to the stealer.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1090.003 T1041
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A developer legitimately downloading the Tor Browser bundle from archive.torproject.org
  • Privacy-conscious user running Tor connectivity checks against check.torproject.org
  • Security research host intentionally connecting to Tor infrastructure
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("tor.exe","firefox.exe","tor-browser.exe","chrome.exe","msedge.exe") and RemoteUrl in~ ("archive.torproject.org","check.torproject.org"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process — if it is a temp-dir dotfile or node child rather than a browser/tor client, treat as malicious; the two raw IPs have no legitimate use. 2) Contain: block the two IPs at egress (already on StepSecurity's global list), isolate the host, and kill the initiating process. 3) Hunt: correlate to the intro.js file-drop and payload-hash UCs on the same host, and rotate all browser credentials given the stealer capability.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in ("37.27.122.124","57.128.246.79")
    or RemoteUrl in~ ("archive.torproject.org","check.torproject.org")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DstIpAddr in ("37.27.122.124","57.128.246.79") or DstHostname in~ ("archive.torproject.org","check.torproject.org")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, DstHostname, SrcHostname, SrcUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Temp-dropped binary reading browser credential and wallet vault stores AIActions on Objectives Medium
Hunts the jscrambler stealer's collection behaviour: a process launched from the OS temp directory (the dropped dotfile payload) opening Chromium/Firefox credential stores (Login Data, Cookies, Web Data, key4.db) or the LevelDB stores where wallet extensions like MetaMask persist their vault. Article-specific because it pairs the temp-dir origin with the exact store filenames the binary embeds engines for. Rationale: Pairs the article's explicit stealer store list (Login Data, Cookies, Web Data, key4.db) with the temp-dir dotfile process origin, so it fires on the stealer's collection step rather than legitimate browser self-access.
ATT&CKT1555.003 T1539 T1005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A portable browser or backup utility run from a temp/extracted folder legitimately reading its own profile
  • Browser credential-migration tooling launched from a temp installer directory
  • Forensic/DFIR collection tool copying browser stores from a temp working path
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is the dropped dotfile (name begins with a dot, in temp) and correlate its hash to the known payloads. 2) Contain: isolate the host, kill the process, and force rotation of all credentials the browser held plus any wallet seed phrases/extension vaults. 3) Hunt: check for outbound exfil to the C2 IPs and review the host for the intro.js container to confirm the jscrambler 8.14.0 root cause.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","key4.db")
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", "/tmp/", "/var/folders/")
| where tostring(split(replace_string(InitiatingProcessFolderPath, "/", "\\"), "\\")[-1]) startswith "."
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","Web Data","key4.db")
| where ActingProcessName has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\Local\Temp\", "/tmp/", "/var/folders/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest

| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02

    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: |

    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or SHA1 in~ ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or MD5 in~ ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or SHA1 in~ ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd") or MD5 in~ ("fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["fbbcf4d8f98168f78f5c0c47a9ae56d59ec8ac84a7c9ca6b797fedfb8d62d2bd", "b7ca95d1b23c8e67416a25cedf741de0917c2096bbc9d24649eea7853d054903", "c8fd47d36bdf7c825378593ab82ed8c24d1dc52e26b507812393e24e1d5201fd"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

2026-07-11 9 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Zimbra is urging customers to apply updates to address a critical security vulnerability impacting the Classic Web Client that could result in arbitrary code execution. The vulnerability has been described as a case of stored cross-site scripting (XSS) that could allow specially crafted emails to execute malicious scripts in a user's session.
